The climate in Sozopol

Sozopol is about 28 m above sea level. The warmest month is August, with an average high of 27°C; the coldest is January, when nights average 2°C. Around 740 mm of precipitation falls in a year on average, most of it in November (about 90 mm).

Sozopol is on a small peninsula on the southern Black Sea coast and has one of the mildest climates in Bulgaria: winters are warm for the country, and frosts are rare. Summers are sunny and dry, and the sea is usually warm enough for swimming from June to the end of September. Autumn is long and warm, but that is also when Mediterranean cyclones bring the most rain.
